title: MDP → DP → MC → TD: The Reinforcement Learning Race Card
subject: Deep Reinforcement Learning
targetAudience: Postgraduate students revising the core progression from Markov decision processes through dynamic programming, Monte Carlo, and temporal-difference learning before exams.
summary: A cross-lecture race card that lines up the four foundational pillars of reinforcement learning — MDPs, Dynamic Programming, Monte Carlo, and Temporal-Difference learning — and races them side by side on model knowledge, bootstrapping, updates, and when to reach for each. Use it as a last-mile revision map that connects Lectures 1–3, 6–7, and 9–10.
keyConcepts: Place each method on the model-based ↔ model-free spectrum and explain what that implies for planning versus learning.
Contrast bootstrapping (DP, TD) with Monte Carlo's reliance on complete returns.
Map each algorithm to the lecture that introduces it and to the problem it solves.
Avoid the common mistake of applying Monte Carlo to continuing tasks or TD to episodes with unknown terminal states.
